title: ASEAN, US adopt principles to combat online scams --Marcos
summary: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on Tuesday announced that the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and the United States have adopted principles to combat online scams, along with a…

blocks.text: Published November 17, 2026 10:50pm

President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on Tuesday announced that the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and the United States have adopted principles to combat online scams, along with a statement outlining 10 principles for public-private partnerships to address the growing threat.
Marcos made the announcement during the ASEAN-US Special Summit in Manila, attended by US President Donald Trump and other ASEAN leaders.

The Philippine president described the adoption of the principles and the statement as an immediate and concrete outcome of the special summit, emphasizing the importance of delivering results beyond diplomatic discussions.

“In anticipation of your arrival, Mr. President, and knowing your desire for results and not just talk, our staffs have been working together, ASEAN and your staffs have been working together, and we have come to being able to finalize and have adopted the principles to tackle online scams,” Marcos said.
He added that the participating governments had also adopted “a statement on ten public-private partnership principles on tackling online scams and the comprehensive work plan.”
“And so that is an immediate result of this special summit between ASEAN and the United States,” he said.
The announcement highlights the importance of closer cooperation between governments and the private sector in addressing online scams, which have become a growing concern across Southeast Asia.
Marcos did not elaborate on the specific provisions of the adopted principles during his remarks.
The announcement came as ASEAN and the United States sought to strengthen their partnership across various areas, including trade, investment, technology and security.
Marcos welcomed Trump’s participation in the summit, saying the US presence reaffirmed the longstanding partnership between Washington and the Southeast Asian bloc.
“Your presence confirms what we already know, that ASEAN and the United States are partners in shaping the region’s future,” Marcos said.
The Philippine president also underscored the deep ties between Manila and Washington, noting that the two countries are marking 80 years of diplomatic relations this year.
He said the relationship is anchored on shared history, values and the enduring connections between their peoples, including millions of Filipinos and Filipino-Americans.
For the Philippines, he said, the partnership with the United States extends to practically every aspect of national life.

“When I’m asked what the most important part of your relationship with the United States is, I cannot answer the question because there is no part of our lives in the Philippines that is not involved with the United States in some way, in some shape or form or another,” Marcos said.
Next year, ASEAN and the United States will mark 50 years of dialogue relations and five years of their Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.
Marcos said he looked forward to further strengthening the relationship between ASEAN and the United States, as well as the bilateral partnership between the Philippines and Washington.
“We look forward to celebrating all the milestones between ASEAN and the United States and the Philippines and the United States,” he said.
“We look forward to continuing to have you as our friend and as our partner," he added. —LDF, GMA News
